headline: High risk: CrewAI’s default shared workspace and broad egress can leak or misroute MemMachine context; prompt-injection and cascading errors are also plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI reads and writes the host working directory and uses stdin/stdout, while MemMachine exposes an MCP server and conversational context. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if MemMachine output is fed into CrewAI tools or files. No direct shared-channel proof is provided, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF MemMachine output is written into CrewAI-readable files or prompts, injection becomes actionable.
IF a shared MCP or file bridge is configured between the agents, attacker-controlled text can steer CrewAI.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Disable automatic file ingestion in CrewAI workflows.
Add a human review step before CrewAI consumes MemMachine output.
Use allowlisted prompt templates for any cross-agent handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data, API keys, and broad network egress; MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context and can expose them through REST, SDK, or MCP. If they share a workspace or hand off context, sensitive data can flow from one to the other in default-like setups. The pairwise leak path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF CrewAI receives MemMachine context as input, that context may be sent onward through CrewAI tools or model providers.
IF both agents operate on the same host workspace, files containing user facts can be read by CrewAI.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and credentials.
Redact secrets before passing data between agents.
Turn off unnecessary tool integrations in CrewAI.
Restrict MemMachine API access to the minimum needed scope.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data classification and filtering.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, write the filesystem, and use broad network egress; MemMachine can use MCP and allowlisted network egress. Their write and network surfaces overlap on shared mutable resources, so concurrent actions can conflict even without git access. The profiles do not show locking, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or stale reads can occur.
IF both agents call the same MCP-backed resource concurrently, state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize writes to shared resources.
Use file locks around any shared artifacts.
Limit CrewAI shell actions to read-only commands where possible.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate tool outputs and act through configured integrations, while MemMachine exposes conversational context and MCP access. If MemMachine output is treated as authoritative by CrewAI, errors can cascade into downstream actions. There is no evidence of built-in verification between them, so the interaction is plausible and medium severity.
conditions: IF CrewAI consumes MemMachine output without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF CrewAI is configured to take external actions based on that output, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking.
Require source citations for all MemMachine-derived claims.
Use a second model or rule-based checker for critical outputs.
Disable automatic execution of MemMachine-supplied instructions.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rollback logic.

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. If the pair is used on regulated or retention-sensitive data, mismatched logging or retention policies can create compliance gaps. The profiles do not document a shared residency or certification mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through both agents, retention and logging must be aligned.
IF either agent persists conversational context longer than the other, deletion/export obligations can diverge.
mitigations: Review retention settings for both systems.
Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Document data-flow boundaries and owners.
Purge stored conversations on a fixed schedule.
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export propagation across both systems.
